questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Use a table of values to find the solution of 2^x = 3x between x = 3 and x = 4, to the nearest tenth.
questions.prompt_markup: Use a table of values to find the solution of 2^x = 3x between x = 3 and x = 4, to the nearest tenth.
questions.required_method: A table of 2^x and 3x at x-values that bracket the solution closely enough to decide the tenth (for example x = 3.3 and x = 3.35), showing where 2^x - 3x changes sign.
questions.grading_note: Form required: rounded to the nearest tenth, with the table. At 3.3, 2^x ≈ 9.85 < 9.9 = 3x; at 3.35, 2^x ≈ 10.20 > 10.05 = 3x, so the solution (about 3.31) rounds to 3.3.

questions.prompt_markup:
The table shows f(x) = |x - 1| and g(x) = 3 - x.
For which x is f(x) = g(x)?
questions.grading_note: At x = 2 both equal 1. In every other column the outputs differ.

questions.skill: Explain why intersections of y = f(x) and y = g(x) solve f(x) = g(x), and approximate solutions with graphs and tables
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x) meet are the solutions of f(x) = g(x).
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x) meet are the solutions of f(x) = g(x).
questions.correct_answer: At a meeting point (a, b), b = f(a) and b = g(a), so f(a) = g(a). If f(a) = g(a), the point (a, f(a)) is on both graphs.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation that uses the coordinates of a point on both graphs.
